forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news.title: ‘I don’t know where the kids will go’: beloved football cage in east London to be demolished
news.summary:
Hackney council will close Keith Miller sports pitch at end of year to build urgently needed social homes

Campaigners say the loss of a much-loved football pitch in east London to a housebuilding programme will be a huge blow to the local community.

Hackney’s Keith Miller sports pitch is known locally as the “San Siro of east London” – for non-football fans, that’s the famous Milan stadium that is one of the biggest in Europe. The Hackney version, however, is due to be demolished at the end of the year so that urgently needed social homes can be built.

news_drafts.headline: Hackney defers £289m of capital spending as major programmes slip
news_drafts.lead: Hackney Council has deferred £288.5m of capital investment planned for 2026/27 to later years, with most of the money pushed back to 2027/28. The deferral signals material disruption to the council's planned spending on long-lived assets — buildings, roads and equipment — across multiple major programmes. The council's strategy to reduce temporary accommodation reliance through acquiring and refurbishing homes has accumulated £189.6m in unspent budgets, with a further £39.2m deferred from this year. Six major housing regeneration schemes show consistent patterns of unspent money: Colville Phase 2C has carried forward £42.6m, Nightingale Block E £23.4m, Kings Crescent Phase 3+4 £18.1m, Buckland Street £16.9m, Fairbank £20.1m and Wimbourne Street £15.2m. The scale and breadth of slippage across independent projects suggests a programme-wide capacity issue rather than isolated delays.

findings.headline: New 2026 regulations mandate independent governance review linked to valuation cycle by 31 March 2028
findings.detail: The regulatory environment is tightening, with new 2026 LGPS regulations requiring funds to complete an independent governance review linked to the triennial valuation cycle. Hackney must meet the 31 March 2028 deadline as part of broader 'Fit for the Future' compliance requirements.
findings.matters: New regulatory compliance deadlines create obligations for funds; reflects broader government consolidation and restructuring of LGPS governance
findings.quote: new 2026 regulations mandated an independent governance review linked to the valuation cycle by 31 March 2028.

findings.headline: UK equities allocation of 32.7% underperforming against benchmark despite diversification strategy
findings.detail: The pension fund's UK equities exposure has risen to 32.7% following new equity and government bond investments. Despite ongoing benchmarking and diversification efforts, this allocation is underperforming its targets.
findings.matters: Significant allocation to underperforming asset class affects funding progress and, ultimately, contribution rate requirements
findings.quote: The pension fund's UK equities exposure had risen to 32.7% due to new equity and government bond investments. Despite benchmarking, equities had underperformed.

findings.headline: System migration from Equinity to LPPA requires rework of CARE calculations due to data integrity gaps
findings.detail: Migration to the LPPA pension administration system revealed that Equinity had retained CARE figures separately from scheme members' records. The initial bulk calculation method failed to account for changes like back pay and salary variations, requiring complete recalculation. This highlights data quality challenges in major system transitions.
findings.matters: Pension administration data integrity directly affects benefit payment accuracy; system migration data issues create risk of payment errors and member disputes
findings.figures: Calculation methodology failure requiring complete rework
findings.quote: Equiniti did not have CARE figures in scheme members' records as they had been retained separately in the Equiniti systems. When the data was transferred to the LPPA, they were unable to upload it directly and they were now redoing bulk calculations as the initial method failed to account for changes like back pay or salary variations.

findings.headline: Government-approved councillor pension access effective 11 May 2026 requires council budget provisioning
findings.detail: Following government approval of councillor pension access, the council has made budget provisions in its medium-term financial planning and amended its elected Members allowances scheme. The expected cost impact is described as not significant.
findings.matters: New government-mandated financial obligations require council budget provisioning; all councils implementing this feature must build it into medium-term plans
findings.quote: Following the government approval of councillor pension access effective from 11 May 2026, it was explained that the money expected was not a significant amount and that the Council had made budget provisions in the medium-term financial planning process and amended the elected Members allowances scheme.

findings.headline: Pension fund contributions fall below pensioner payouts through 2027, marking fund maturation
findings.detail: The fund is experiencing contributions received falling short of pensioner payouts through 2027, a natural phase in pension fund maturation as pensioner numbers rise. The fund manages this through daily monitoring and adequate cash reserves plus income-generating assets to avoid forced divestment.
findings.matters: Negative cash flow phases require careful liquidity and asset management; funds shifting from contribution-positive to contribution-negative lifecycle phase face different risk management requirements
findings.quote: the contributions received against pensioners payout mismatch through 2027 reflected the natural maturation of LGPS funds with rising pensioner numbers. There was daily monitoring of the issue, noting that ample cash reserves and income-generating assets prevented the need for divestment to cover shortfalls.
